name: Chaotic academia

lead: Chaotic academia is an internet aesthetic descended from dark academia, the literary, university-inspired look. It keeps the cardigans, blazers and tweed but leans into mismatch, layering and clutter.
The appearance payoff is a lived-in, creative scholar look: patterned pieces, accessories and well-worn textures that read as personality rather than polish.

paras: People combine thrifted tweed, knitwear, shirts, scarves and bags in layered, deliberately uncoordinated outfits in earthy colours, often with books and stationery as props.
Style only; there are no health risks specific to it. Critics of the wider dark academia scene cite elitism and a glamorisation of overwork.

angle.text: The look changes how a person dresses, using layering, texture and accessories to project a bookish, bohemian personality.

lead: Chaotic academia is one of several variants of dark academia, the internet aesthetic centred on higher education, literature and the arts that emerged on Tumblr around 2014-2015 and grew sharply during the early 2020s.[1] Wikipedia names it alongside gothic academia and green academia as aesthetics that followed the subculture's growth, without describing it in detail.[1]

Dark academia itself is described as maximalist and nostalgic, drawing on 1930s and 1940s Oxbridge and Ivy League fashion with cardigans, blazers, Oxford shoes, houndstooth and tweed in browns, blacks, beiges and dark green.[1] Chaotic academia is generally understood as the messier, more eclectic end of that look, built on layering and mismatch.

paras: Dark academia grew from fans of Donna Tartt's 1992 novel The Secret History on Tumblr, spread to Instagram and Pinterest around 2017 and to TikTok during the pandemic.[1] Chaotic academia is among the later sub-aesthetics.[1]
